---
title: "B · Footprints & PSF — methods"
---

## Pixel size from view geometry

A cross-track scanner samples in **angle**: every pixel subtends the same angular width α along-scan
and δ along-track. On a spherical Earth of radius R, seen from altitude h at scan angle θ:

$$
\eta = \arcsin\!\Big(\tfrac{R+h}{R}\sin\theta\Big),\qquad
r = (R+h)\cos\theta - \sqrt{R^2 - (R+h)^2\sin^2\theta},
$$
$$
W_\text{scan} = \frac{r\,\alpha}{\cos\eta},\qquad W_\text{track} = r\,\delta,
$$

with η the view zenith angle at the ground and r the slant range. The along-scan size grows both
with range and with the oblique incidence (1/cos η); the along-track size only with range. For
real pixels we use the product's own view zenith and the satellite radius from the orbit data:
r = √(R<sub>s</sub>² − R² sin²η) − R cos η, which handles altitude changes (e.g. the lowered Terra/Aqua
orbits) automatically.

| | altitude | α (along-scan) | δ (along-track) | nadir | swath edge |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MODIS 1 km | 705 km | 1.418 mrad | 1.418 mrad | 1.0 × 1.0 km | 4.8 × 2.0 km (55°) |
| VIIRS M | 829 km | 0.312 mrad × aggregation (3/2/1) | 0.891 mrad | 0.78 × 0.74 km | 1.6 × 1.6 km (56°) |
| ECOSTRESS | ~400–420 km | 0.171 mrad | 0.185 mrad | 69 × 77 m | ~90 × 90 m (25.5°) |

VIIRS keeps its pixels nearly square by **aggregating** 3, 2 or 1 native samples on board depending
on scan angle (zones at 31.59° and 44.68°), so its along-scan size jumps at the zone boundaries rather
than growing smoothly.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
presets = ({MODIS: {h: 705, a: 1.418, d: 1.418, max: 55}, "VIIRS M": {h: 829, a: 0.312, d: 0.891, max: 56.06},
            ECOSTRESS: {h: 415, a: 0.171, d: 0.185, max: 25.5}})
viewof preset = Inputs.radio(Object.keys(presets), {value: "MODIS", label: "sensor preset"})
viewof hkm = Inputs.range([300, 900], {value: presets[preset].h, step: 1, label: "altitude (km)"})
viewof alpha = Inputs.range([0.1, 2], {value: presets[preset].a, step: 0.001, label: "α along-scan (mrad)"})
viewof delta = Inputs.range([0.1, 2], {value: presets[preset].d, step: 0.001, label: "δ along-track (mrad)"})
viewof thSel = Inputs.range([0, presets[preset].max], {value: presets[preset].max * 0.8, step: 0.1, label: "scan angle (°)"})
fpCurve = {
  const R = 6371, out = [];
  for (let t = 0; t <= presets[preset].max; t += 0.25) {
    const th = t * Math.PI / 180, Rs = R + hkm, eta = Math.asin(Math.min(1, Rs / R * Math.sin(th)));
    const r = Rs * Math.cos(th) - Math.sqrt(Math.max(0, R * R - Rs * Rs * Math.sin(th) ** 2));
    const agg = preset === "VIIRS M" ? (t < 31.59 ? 3 : t < 44.68 ? 2 : 1) : 1;
    out.push({theta: t, km: r * alpha * agg / 1000 / Math.cos(eta), axis: "along-scan"});
    out.push({theta: t, km: r * delta / 1000, axis: "along-track"});
  }
  return out;
}
fpAt = fpCurve.filter(d => Math.abs(d.theta - Math.round(thSel * 4) / 4) < 1e-6)
```

::: {.widget}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({height: 260, marginLeft: 50, x: {label: "scan angle (°)"}, y: {label: "pixel size (km)", zero: true},
  color: {domain: ["along-scan", "along-track"], range: ["#2a78d6", "#eb6834"], legend: true},
  marks: [Plot.line(fpCurve, {x: "theta", y: "km", stroke: "axis", strokeWidth: 2}),
          Plot.ruleX([thSel], {stroke: "#898781"}),
          Plot.dot(fpAt, {x: "theta", y: "km", fill: "axis", r: 5, tip: true})]})
```
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({height: 200, width: 360, aspectRatio: 1, x: {label: "along-scan (km)", domain: [-3, 3]}, y: {label: "along-track (km)", domain: [-3, 3]},
  marks: [Plot.rect([{x1: -0.5, x2: 0.5, y1: -0.5, y2: 0.5}], {x1: "x1", x2: "x2", y1: "y1", y2: "y2", stroke: "#898781", fill: "none"}),
          Plot.rect([{x1: -fpAt[0].km / 2, x2: fpAt[0].km / 2, y1: -fpAt[1].km / 2, y2: fpAt[1].km / 2}],
                    {x1: "x1", x2: "x2", y1: "y1", y2: "y2", fill: "#2a78d6", fillOpacity: 0.25, stroke: "#2a78d6"}),
          Plot.text([`${fpAt[0].km.toFixed(2)} × ${fpAt[1].km.toFixed(2)} km`], {frameAnchor: "top-left", dx: 6, dy: 6})]})
```
Grey square: 1 km reference.
:::

## Bow-tie: overlapping scans

Each scan covers a strip `N_det` detectors wide. At nadir consecutive strips just touch; because the
strip widens with range while the spacecraft advances a fixed distance per scan, strips **overlap**
off-nadir — by ~50 % at the MODIS swath edge. MODIS keeps all overlapping pixels (so a ground point can
be in two pixels of different scans); VIIRS deletes the duplicated edge detectors on board ("bow-tie
deletion", which is why VNP21 has fill values at the edges of scans off-nadir); ECOSTRESS scans overlap by
15–30 L1B lines.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof btTheta = Inputs.range([0, 55], {value: 50, step: 1, label: "MODIS scan angle (°)"})
btOverlap = {
  const R = 6371, h = 705, th = btTheta * Math.PI / 180, Rs = R + h;
  const r = Rs * Math.cos(th) - Math.sqrt(R * R - Rs * Rs * Math.sin(th) ** 2);
  const strip = r * 1.418e-3 * 10; // km, 10 detectors
  return {strip, overlap: Math.max(0, 1 - 10 / strip)};
}
btRects = d3.range(4).map(k => ({k, y1: k * 10 - btOverlap.strip / 2 + 5, y2: k * 10 + btOverlap.strip / 2 + 5}))
```

::: {.widget}
At ${btTheta}° each scan's strip is **${btOverlap.strip.toFixed(1)} km** long along-track but the spacecraft advances
only 10 km per scan: **${(100 * btOverlap.overlap).toFixed(0)} %** overlap.
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({height: 180, x: {label: "along-scan (arbitrary)", domain: [0, 1], axis: null}, y: {label: "along-track (km)", domain: [-15, 50]},
  color: {range: ["#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#eda100"]},
  marks: [Plot.rect(btRects, {x1: 0.1, x2: 0.9, y1: "y1", y2: "y2", fill: "k", fillOpacity: 0.3, stroke: "k"})]})
```
:::

## Voronoi cells

Nearest-neighbour extraction implicitly assigns every ground point to the closest pixel centre:
the **Voronoi cell** of that centre. It is therefore the "pixel" that point-extraction code
actually uses. We build planar Voronoi diagrams of pixel centres in a local Lambert
equal-area projection (`shapely.voronoi_polygons`). Voronoi cells tile the plane without
overlap and adapt automatically to growing pixel spacing — so their areas match the
trigonometric footprints well where scans do not overlap. In bow-tie zones they shrink and
become slivers (two centres from different scans sit close together), and they never include the
PSF tails. They need no sensor model at all, only the centres.

## Point spread functions

The radiance assigned to a pixel is a weighted average of the scene under the instrument's
**PSF**, which is wider than the nominal footprint. We model each PSF as separable
along-scan × along-track, each axis a convolution of boxes and Gaussians in units of the pixel's
own sample spacing (so it automatically stretches with view angle). Values and sources
(full references below; see `config/psf.toml`):

* **MODIS** bands 31/32: along-scan = detector box ⊗ scan-motion box = **triangle** (FWHM 1, base 2 samples;
  ~75 % of the signal from the nominal pixel) ⊗ optical blur; along-track ≈ box ⊗ blur. Blur Gaussians fitted to the
  measured pre-launch MTF at Nyquist (0.34–0.37 scan, 0.54–0.55 track) [B98, Tan06].
* **VIIRS** M15/M16: along-scan = box(1) ⊗ native sample trapezoid of width 1/k for aggregation k = 3, 2, 1
  (MTF<sub>N</sub> measured 0.59/0.54/0.35 vs. ideal 0.58/0.52/0.405); along-track ≈ box ("essentially square") [Lin13, W13].
* **ECOSTRESS**: the ideal geometric response would be ~1 sample wide, but on-orbit bridge transects
  show a **Gaussian with FWHM 157 m (along-track) × 162 m (across)** — about **twice** the 70 m sample spacing [H24].

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
function rect(w) { return u => (Math.abs(u) <= w / 2 ? 1 : 0) }
function gauss(f) { const s = f / 2.355; return u => Math.exp(-0.5 * (u / s) ** 2) }
function conv(fs, du = 0.01, L = 4) {
  const n = Math.round(2 * L / du) + 1, xs = d3.range(n).map(i => -L + i * du);
  let cur = null;
  for (const f of fs) {
    let k = xs.map(f); const s = d3.sum(k); k = k.map(v => v / s);
    if (!cur) { cur = k; continue; }
    const out = new Array(n).fill(0), h = (n - 1) / 2;
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) for (let j = 0; j < n; j++) { const m = i + j - h; if (m >= 0 && m < n) out[m] += cur[i] * k[j]; }
    cur = out;
  }
  const s = d3.sum(cur); return xs.map((x, i) => ({u: x, f: cur[i] / s / du}));
}
psfDefs = ({
  "MODIS": {s: [rect(1), rect(1), gauss(0.377)], t: [rect(1), gauss(0.412)]},
  "VIIRS (3:1 zone)": {s: [rect(1), rect(1/3), rect(1/3)], t: [rect(1)]},
  "VIIRS (1:1 zone)": {s: [rect(1), rect(1), gauss(0.3)], t: [rect(1)]},
  "ECOSTRESS (measured)": {s: [gauss(2.36)], t: [gauss(2.07)]},
  "Box (no PSF)": {s: [rect(1)], t: [rect(1)]}})
viewof psfSel = Inputs.select(Object.keys(psfDefs), {value: "MODIS", label: "PSF"})
lsfS = conv(psfDefs[psfSel].s)
lsfT = conv(psfDefs[psfSel].t)
inPix = a => d3.sum(a.filter(d => Math.abs(d.u) <= 0.5), d => d.f) * 0.01
```

::: {.widget}
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({height: 240, x: {label: "distance from pixel centre (samples)", domain: [-3, 3]}, y: {label: "response"},
  color: {domain: ["along-scan", "along-track"], range: ["#2a78d6", "#eb6834"], legend: true},
  marks: [Plot.rectY([{x1: -0.5, x2: 0.5}], {x1: "x1", x2: "x2", y: 1.05, fill: "#e1e0d9", fillOpacity: 0.5}),
          Plot.line(lsfS, {x: "u", y: "f", stroke: () => "along-scan"}),
          Plot.line(lsfT, {x: "u", y: "f", stroke: () => "along-track"})]})
```
Energy from inside the nominal pixel: along-scan **${(100 * inPix(lsfS)).toFixed(0)} %**, along-track
**${(100 * inPix(lsfT)).toFixed(0)} %**, so the nominal footprint holds only **${(100 * inPix(lsfS) * inPix(lsfT)).toFixed(0)} %** of the signal
(grey band = nominal pixel).
:::

## Areal averages: weighting schemes

For a polygon A the areal mean is estimated as Σ w<sub>i</sub> x<sub>i</sub> / Σ w<sub>i</sub>. We compare:

| Scheme | weight w<sub>i</sub> | assumption |
|---|---|---|
| Centre in polygon | 1 if the centre is in A | pixels are points |
| Nominal square | area of (nadir-size square at the centre) ∩ A | all pixels the same size |
| Voronoi | area of (Voronoi cell) ∩ A | nearest-neighbour partition |
| Trig footprint | area of (footprint quadrilateral) ∩ A | true size, overlap double-counted |
| Trig footprint, overlap-aware | ∫<sub>A</sub> b<sub>i</sub> / Σ<sub>j</sub> b<sub>j</sub> | true size; overlapping footprints share the ground |
| PSF | \|F<sub>i</sub>\| ∫<sub>A</sub> p<sub>i</sub> | true size + PSF, overlap double-counted |
| PSF, overlap-aware | ∫<sub>A</sub> p<sub>i</sub> / Σ<sub>j</sub> p<sub>j</sub> | true size + PSF ("partition of unity") |

where b<sub>i</sub> is the box PSF of footprint i and p<sub>i</sub> the sensor PSF (both normalised). The
overlap-aware forms let every point of A distribute its unit area among the pixels that see it,
in proportion to how strongly each sees it; their weights sum to the polygon area exactly. They are
integrated by quadrature in each pixel's own frame, with the denominator accumulated on a fine
raster in a local equal-area plane (node spacing adapted to the largest pixel so the raster has no holes).

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof aLo = Inputs.range([0, 20], {value: 6.3, step: 0.1, label: "polygon start (km)"})
viewof aHi = Inputs.range([0, 20], {value: 9.1, step: 0.1, label: "polygon end (km)"})
viewof growth = Inputs.range([1, 5], {value: 3, step: 0.1, label: "pixel growth across the line"})
pix1d = {
  // pixels along a line whose size grows linearly (like a swath towards its edge)
  const out = []; let x = 0, i = 0;
  while (x < 20) { const w = 0.6 * (1 + (growth - 1) * x / 20); out.push({i, x0: x, x1: x + w, c: x + w / 2, w}); x += w; i++; }
  return out;
}
field = x => 300 + 8 * Math.sin(x * 1.3) + (x > 8 ? 6 : 0)
obs1d = pix1d.map(p => { // triangle PSF of base 2 samples
  let s = 0, n = 0; for (let u = -1; u <= 1; u += 0.02) { const wt = 1 - Math.abs(u); s += wt * field(p.c + u * p.w); n += wt; }
  return {...p, x: s / n};
})
truth1d = { let s = 0, n = 0; for (let x = aLo; x < aHi; x += 0.001) { s += field(x); n++; } return n ? s / n : NaN; }
schemes1d = {
  const lo = Math.min(aLo, aHi), hi = Math.max(aLo, aHi), ov = (a, b) => Math.max(0, Math.min(b, hi) - Math.max(a, lo));
  const est = w => { const sw = d3.sum(w); return sw ? d3.sum(obs1d.map((p, i) => w[i] * p.x)) / sw : NaN; };
  return [
    {scheme: "Centre in polygon", est: est(obs1d.map(p => (p.c >= lo && p.c <= hi ? 1 : 0)))},
    {scheme: "Nominal size (0.6 km)", est: est(obs1d.map(p => ov(p.c - 0.3, p.c + 0.3)))},
    {scheme: "True footprint", est: est(obs1d.map(p => ov(p.x0, p.x1)))},
    {scheme: "Footprint + PSF", est: est(obs1d.map(p => { let s = 0; for (let u = -1; u <= 1; u += 0.02) { const x = p.c + u * p.w; if (x >= lo && x <= hi) s += 1 - Math.abs(u); } return s; }))},
  ].map(d => ({...d, err: d.est - truth1d}));
}
```

::: {.widget}
**1-D toy.** Pixels grow ${growth}× from left to right (like a swath edge); the scene has a 6 K step at
x = 8 km; each pixel observes it through a triangular PSF. Drag the polygon over the step and towards the
large pixels.
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({height: 200, x: {label: "x (km)", domain: [0, 20]}, y: {label: "LST (K)"},
  marks: [Plot.rectY([{a: Math.min(aLo, aHi), b: Math.max(aLo, aHi)}], {x1: "a", x2: "b", y1: 290, y2: 316, fill: "#e34948", fillOpacity: 0.08}),
          Plot.line(d3.range(0, 20, 0.02).map(x => ({x, y: field(x)})), {x: "x", y: "y", stroke: "#898781"}),
          Plot.rect(obs1d, {x1: "x0", x2: "x1", y1: d => d.x - 0.25, y2: d => d.x + 0.25, fill: "#2a78d6"}),
          Plot.tickX(obs1d, {x: "c", y: "x", stroke: "#fcfcfb"})]})
```
```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Inputs.table(schemes1d.map(d => ({Scheme: d.scheme, "Estimate (K)": d.est.toFixed(2), "Error vs truth (K)": d.err.toFixed(2)})), {sort: null})
```
True mean over the polygon: **${truth1d.toFixed(2)} K**. (Even the best scheme cannot fully undo the PSF:
it recovers the mean of the *blurred* scene.)
:::

## Synthetic-truth test

Real LST has no known truth, so we also simulated it: the 70 m ECOSTRESS LST of the same afternoon
(gaps filled with the nearest valid value) is treated as the true field. Every MODIS/VIIRS pixel of
the real scenes "observes" it through its trigonometric footprint and PSF (31 × 31 quadrature
nodes, nearest 70 m pixel). For 60 random squares and circles of 2, 5, 10 and 20 km, each weighting
scheme estimates the polygon mean, compared with the mean of the 70 m pixels inside it. This isolates
the effect of the pixel model (no retrieval error, no time difference, no geolocation error).

* [W13] Wolfe et al. (2013) Suomi NPP VIIRS prelaunch and on-orbit geometric calibration and characterization. *JGR-Atmos.* 118:11508.
* [VGeoATBD] NASA (2014) Revised JPSS VIIRS Geolocation ATBD (423-ATBD-002).
* [H24] Holmes et al. (2024) On-orbit spatial performance characterization for thermal infrared imagers of Landsat 7, 8, and 9, ECOSTRESS and CTI. *JGR-Biogeosciences* 129, e2023JG007506.
